blocks.text: Chennai Photo Biennale & WWF-India present In Dialogue with Nature .
A delicate interplay between wildlife, landscapes, topographies, the human position and connection reveals a shared existence, recognising that we shape the world as much as the world shapes us.

Through intimate encounters, quiet observation, and layered visual narratives, the works invite viewers to consider landscapes as more than mere backdrops to human life, and wildlife as more than exotic species. They foreground humanity’s role and influence within the natural world, positioning us as active collaborators in shaping stories of curiosity, restraint, and interdependence.

The artists invite us to slow down and observe the small, often overlooked acts through which humans, animals, and ecosystems coexist, sometimes in harmony, sometimes in resistance. The artworks hold together beauty and unease, revealing how ecological relationships are marked by vulnerability, resilience, and the politics of space.

“A photograph holds far more than a moment in time. It carries traces of place, memory, human presence, and the environment that shapes us all. For us, photography has always been a way of seeing more carefully and engaging more deeply with the world around us. This collaboration between Chennai Photo Biennale and WWF-India grew from a shared belief in the power of images to foster empathy and awareness. At a moment when ecological loss can feel distant or overwhelming, these works bring the conversation closer — grounding it in lived landscapes and human connection. Supporting this project means supporting artists who give form to these stories, and the conservation efforts that safeguard the fragile ecosystems they reflect. We hope this catalogue encourages you to linger, to reflect, and to carry forward a renewed sense of care and responsibility for the world we share.” — Pheroza J. Godrej and Tarana Sawhney
